title: The dimension of a scheme is the supremum of the dimensions of the rings of an affine open cover
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty scheme [def-pc-scheme] and let $(U_i)_{i\in I}$ be a family of open subschemes of $X$ with $X=\bigcup_{i\in I}U_i$, each $U_i$ isomorphic to $\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ for a commutative ring $A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $\dim X$ be the dimension of $X$ [def-pc-dimension] (the supremum of the Krull dimensions of the local rings $\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $x\in X$) and $\dim A_i\in\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ the Krull dimension of the ring $A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then
$$
\dim X=\sup_{i\in I}\dim A_i
$$
in $\{-\infty,0,1,2,\ldots,\infty\}$ (an empty $U_i$ has $A_i=0$ and contributes $-\infty$).

source.place: Properties, Lemma 04MU (properties-lemma-dimension, properties.tex line 1233: dim X = sup of the dimensions of the local rings), together with Schemes, Lemma 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves, schemes.tex line 692: the stalk of the structure sheaf of Spec A at p is A_p) and Algebra, Lemma 00KG (algebra-lemma-dimension-height, algebra.tex line 14353: dim R is the supremum of the heights of its primes); tags verified in stacks-project/tags/tags

proof.text: (Set-up.) Fix $i$ and put $R_i=\mathcal O_X(U_i)$. Since $U_i\cong\operatorname{Spec}A_i$ as schemes, $U_i$ is an affine open of $X$, and applying global sections to this isomorphism gives a ring isomorphism $R_i=\Gamma(U_i,\mathcal O_{U_i})\cong\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}A_i,\mathcal O)=A_i$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. A ring isomorphism carries chains of prime ideals to chains of prime ideals of the same length, so $\dim R_i=\dim A_i$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points] there is an open immersion $\iota_i:\operatorname{Spec}R_i\to X$ with image $U_i$, and for $x\in U_i$ the prime $\mathfrak p_x\subset R_i$ with $\iota_i(\mathfrak p_x)=x$ is unique ($\iota_i$ is injective); conversely every prime $\mathfrak p$ of $R_i$ is $\mathfrak p_x$ for $x=\iota_i(\mathfrak p)\in U_i$. So $x\mapsto\mathfrak p_x$ is a bijection from $U_i$ onto the set of primes of $R_i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves, schemes.tex line 692), parts (1) and (6)

proof.text: (Local rings.) For $x\in U_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c) gives a ring isomorphism $(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$, so $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\dim(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}$ (isomorphic rings have the same chains of primes). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime], $\dim(R_i)_{\mathfrak p_x}=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p_x$, the supremum of the lengths $t$ of chains $\mathfrak q_0\subsetneq\cdots\subsetneq\mathfrak q_t\subseteq\mathfrak p_x$ of primes of $R_i$. Hence $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p_x$ for every $x\in U_i$.

source.place: Schemes, Lemma 01HV (schemes-lemma-spec-sheaves, schemes.tex line 692), parts (1) and (6)

proof.text: (Supremum over one chart.) By step 1, as $x$ runs over $U_i$ the prime $\mathfrak p_x$ runs over all primes of $R_i$, each once. By step 2 and [lem-pc-ring-dimension-supremum-heights] applied to $R_i$, $\sup_{x\in U_i}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\sup_{\mathfrak p\subset R_i\text{ prime}}\operatorname{ht}\mathfrak p=\dim R_i=\dim A_i$, in $\{-\infty,0,1,\ldots,\infty\}$; for $U_i=\emptyset$ both sides are $-\infty$ ($R_i\cong A_i$ has no prime).

source.place: Algebra, Definition 00KF (definition-height, line 14347) and Lemma 00KG (algebra-lemma-dimension-height, line 14353)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) Since $X=\bigcup_iU_i$, the supremum over $x\in X$ splits as a supremum of suprema: $\dim X=\sup_{x\in X}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=\sup_{i\in I}\sup_{x\in U_i}\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}$ (every $x$ lies in some $U_i$, and every term on the right is a term on the left) [def-pc-dimension]; by step 3 this is $\sup_{i\in I}\dim A_i$. ($X\neq\emptyset$ is only needed for $\dim X$ to be defined by [def-pc-dimension]; then some $U_i$ is nonempty and the supremum is $\ge0$.)
